status_summary: The TikTok element went a different way from the recommendation: executive orders delayed enforcement of the 2024 divest-or-ban law, an order published 2025-09-30 described a qualified divestiture process, and a U.S. joint venture deal closed on 2026-01-22 (Politico), so the app was not banned. The FCC elements have advanced: on 2025-12-22 its Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (DA 25-1086) added to the Covered List all foreign-produced drones and drone critical components and the equipment listed in Section 1709 of the FY2025 defense law, following a determination received 2025-12-21 and subject to exceptions the Department of War or Homeland Security may determine; FCC bureaus on 2026-07-06 barred continued import and marketing of previously authorized equipment added to the list in 2024 or earlier; and final rules published 2025-11-25 and 2026-09-11 bar authorizing devices with covered modular transmitters and close a component-part loophole for Covered List entities. A proposal released 2026-05-01 (FCC 26-29, published 2026-05-08) would exclude Covered List entities from blanket domestic Section 214 authority and tentatively treats interconnection with entities that lack or lose that authority as unreasonable, but only asks whether to bar interconnection at their points of presence and data centers, so the chapter's data-center point is a question in a proposal, not a rule; a final rule (FCC 26-2, adopted 2026-01-29, published 2026-04-10, effective 2026-06-09, compliance date to be announced) requires licensees to attest whether they are foreign adversary controlled and treats a 10 percent holder as having control power, without providing for the public list the chapter recommends. On rip-and-replace, Congress authorized the FCC to borrow $3.08 billion in December 2024, before the period tracked, and the FCC announced in April 2025 that it had the funds; a clean standards initiative and an AI plan were not verified.

timeline.event: Presidential document published as Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security: it summarizes the executive orders that delayed enforcement of the divest-or-ban law and describes the qualified divestiture process that could lift the law's prohibitions.
FCC final rule bars authorizing devices that contain covered modular transmitters and adds a procedure to limit prior authorizations of covered equipment.

An FCC bureau notice (DA 25-1086) added foreign-produced drones and drone critical components, and the communications and video surveillance equipment and services listed in Section 1709 of the FY2025 defense law, to the Covered List, based on a national security determination received 2025-12-21, unless the Department of War or Homeland Security determines that a given drone or component does not pose such risks.

TikTok announces that a U.S. joint venture deal valued at $14 billion has closed; Silver Lake, MGX and Oracle each hold 15 percent and the parent company keeps a stake of nearly 20 percent (Politico, republished by Yahoo Finance).

The FCC released its Report and Order on foreign adversary control transparency (FCC 26-2, adopted 2026-01-29), requiring regulated entities to attest whether they are foreign adversary controlled and adopting a uniform 10 percent threshold for presuming control power, after rejecting 5 percent thresholds proposed by commenters.

FCC final rule requires holders of FCC licenses and authorizations to attest whether they are owned or controlled by a foreign adversary and to disclose details if so; effective 2026-06-09, with compliance dates to be announced; a holder of 10 percent or more is presumed to hold control power.

The FCC released a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (FCC 26-29, adopted 2026-04-30) proposing to exclude Covered List entities from blanket domestic Section 214 authority, seeking comment on revoking existing authority, tentatively concluding that interconnection with entities lacking or losing that authority would be unreasonable, and asking whether to bar interconnection at their points of presence and data centers.

The FCC's domestic Section 214 proposal (FCC 26-29) was published in the Federal Register: it would exclude Covered List entities from blanket domestic Section 214 authority, tentatively finds interconnection with entities that lack or lose that authority unreasonable, and asks whether to bar interconnection at their points of presence and data centers.
FCC bureaus bar the continued import and marketing of previously authorized equipment added to the Covered List in 2024 or earlier, acting through a public notice under rule 2.939.
FCC final rule closes a component-part loophole for Covered List entities, requires full certification for their modifications, and requires online marketplaces to display FCC IDs.

title: Ban TikTok and expand FCC restrictions on Chinese-linked equipment and carriers
uncertainties: This record combines a TikTok element that diverged from the recommendation with FCC elements that are partly on track, and the 45 progress figure is a judgment across them. The Covered List page on fcc.gov is an old cached copy; the December 2025 additions were read directly in the bureau's notice (DA 25-1086, opened on docs.fcc.gov on 2026-10-22), but the original Covered List order was not read. An external retrieval also reports later additions of foreign-produced routers (DA 26-278, 2026-03-23) and of power inverters and advanced robotic devices (DA 26-786, 2026-07-28); these were not opened and are not recorded as verified. FCC 26-29 was read on docs.fcc.gov except its last 5,589 characters: its tentative conclusions concern interconnection with entities that lack or lose domestic Section 214 authority, while a bar on interconnection at points of presence and data centers is posed only as a question. The attestation rule's Federal Register text was read in two parts covering the whole document in an earlier review; no public-list provision was seen, though whether the filed attestations or the annual report will be public is not stated. The docs.fcc.gov copy of FCC 26-2 was read in its first 100,000 and last 16,000 characters: it describes a pending bill that would direct a public list of licensees as legislation, not a rule of the order, and the text of its sections on the filing deadline and on publication of data (paragraphs 79 and 97) did not come through, so the public-list question remains unverified from that copy. An external retrieval's statement that all holders of 5 percent or more must be disclosed was not found in the text read; the order rejects 5 percent thresholds proposed by commenters, so that claim stays unverified. A related earlier Commission notice (FCC 25-28) could not be opened. The rip-and-replace funding source is trade press; the borrowing authority date (December 2024) predates the inauguration and disbursement progress was not found. The terms of the TikTok joint venture were taken from a Politico report, not a primary document.
